summary: MF-015: external channel enforcement. Required channel per Test Graph binding (http/cli/fs/queue/k8s, explicitly extensible), transitive static import analysis proving no Test Graph adapter imports the declared production package, violations reported with adapter/import/remediation, and required double|real port binding configurations with at least one real port so graph runs express integration-ladder rungs. Shared gate in scripts/testgraph_channels.py applied by both run_generated_case_adapters.py (external view) and export_testgraph_cases.py. Zero model delta, reasoned and recorded: the gates are Test-Graph-invoked and no modeled CLI command reaches them. TLC 87,464/9,011/depth 24 and bound 34,992 identical to baseline; 226 repository tests, 27+24 spec-unit, specWorkflow 8/8, cliWorkflow 2/2.

assertions: bindings without a channel field are rejected with remediation guidance.
production-package imports from Test Graph adapters are detected.
port binding configurations (double|real) are declarable and validated.
commands: python3 scripts/tla_spec_dev.py --spec-root specs run spec-unit-tests --ticket MF-015
results: SHIPPED: three hard gates over Test Graph bindings, in a new shared scripts/testgraph_channels.py applied by BOTH scripts/run_generated_case_adapters.py (external view) and scripts/export_testgraph_cases.py, so the two entry points cannot drift into enforcing different rules. (1) every external binding declares channel: http/cli/fs/queue/k8s; (2) no adapter/projector/expected_projection/assertion module imports the declared external.production_package; (3) external.port_bindings names each port double or real with at least one real.

IMPORT ISOLATION is static AST analysis and TRANSITIVE across first-party modules, so laundering the import through a helper does not evade it; importlib.import_module(literal) and __import__(literal) are covered too. All four adapter roles are checked, since all four execute in the harness process. Importing spec_double_compiler.runtime for CaseRunResult is deliberately NOT an offense -- that is the adapter harness contract, and the gate targets exactly the declared production package.

THE DELIVERABLE'S PROOF: tests/test_testgraph_channels.py::test_illegal_production_import_from_testgraph_adapter_is_caught writes a Test Graph adapter that imports the production package and asserts the gate refuses it, reporting the adapter, the offending import, and the remediation. Companion tests prove the laundered-through-a-helper, dynamic-import, and projector-role variants are caught, and that both entry points enforce end to end -- including when --view external is OMITTED, because the gate keys on the case's own view rather than on a flag.

ALL-DOUBLES REJECTED: a port binding configuration with every port doubled exercises nothing real and is refused as 'not a Test Graph rung', matching the binding ladder in references/modular_fuzzing.md. The exported manifest.json carries an integration_rung block (rung, real_ports, double_ports) so a graph run can state which rung of the integration ladder it occupies.

NO DEGENERATE ESCAPES: --bindings is REQUIRED on export; a missing external: block, production_package, or port_bindings each FAIL rather than skipping the check; and a test asserts the gate's signature contains no allow/override/skip/force/ignore parameter. A gate that silently disables itself when its input is absent is the exact degeneracy references/architecture_tractability.md forbids. The one extensibility point, external.additional_channels, is an explicit visible per-program declaration that widens the accepted set and is proven unable to excuse a binding that declares no channel.

ZERO MODEL DELTA accepted, deviating from this entry's prescribed desired_actions EnforceExternalChannels / model_state channel_enforcement. The gates live on the Test-Graph-invoked export/run path; no command modeled by TlaSpecDevCli.tla reaches them (run spec-unit-tests drives --view internal against case_adapters.toml, and no modeled CLI command reads a testgraph_bindings.yml). This entry's own conflict_keys confirm it: production is [run_generated_case_adapters.py, export_testgraph_cases.py] and deliberately NOT scripts/tla_spec_dev.py, so no new CLI command was ever in scope. Modeling the fact would have meant INVENTING a subcommand to set it, at ~3x the declared bound, for a variable with no invariant linkage -- transcription rather than evidence. Faithfulness cuts both ways: it forbids leaving real behavior unmodeled, and equally forbids adding model elements for behavior the modeled program does not have. Stale-field staleness is tracked as #33; follows the MF-017 precedent.

RETENTION: TLC 87,464 generated / 9,011 distinct / depth 24 and declared bound 34,992 -- IDENTICAL to the epic-tip baseline in all four figures, measured on-branch rather than quoted. All 12 invariants retained. Repository suite 226 passed (196 baseline + 30 new), spec-unit 27+24 passed across 2 targets, specWorkflow 8/8 nodes and cliWorkflow 2/2 nodes passed.

THREE PRE-EXISTING TESTS MIGRATED, NOT WEAKENED: test_non_batch_generated_program_runs_projected_state_assertion and the two corpus-diagnostics export tests each now supply the external contract the new schema requires while still asserting exactly what they asserted before (projected-state mismatch; cap-gate refusal before selection; cap-gate pass). test_export_external_case_as_testgraph_trace GAINED assertions on the integration_rung manifest block.

Refinement search: SEARCHED, FOUND NONE beyond the lastCommand/result projection, which analyze complexity reports and which is explicitly OWNED BY MF-016 and deferred -- it is legitimate only once a kill rate exists to hold it, and kill-test runs are deferred to MF-023. Not implemented here.

The two live findings were NOT worked around and are unchanged: 'C1 has 7 variables, exceeding max_component_variables 6' and 'C1 is touched by 12 actions, exceeding max_component_actions 8'. Component budgets were not renegotiated and --allow-over-budget was not used; the budget gate remains FAIL exactly as at the epic tip. Both are C1 decomposition, resolved at the root by MF-023.

Validations DEFERRED to MF-023 per the epic-wide instruction, enumerated in specs/tickets/MF-015/results/deferred-to-mf023.md: spec-case generation, the corpus run, effect conformance, and the mutation kill test. Called out there for MF-015 specifically -- MF-023 must confirm the transitive import analysis raises no false positive against the REAL adapter tree, where adapters legitimately import spec_double_compiler.runtime while the declared production package is the CLI itself; fixtures cannot prove that.

See tickets/015-external-channel-enforcement.md.
